2027-05-06.title: Suloko · The Ascension of our Lord
readings: The tablets placed in the ark
Elijah taken up; Elisha takes his mantle
I will write my law on their hearts
He was lifted up, and a cloud took him
He blessed them and was carried up into heaven
2027-05-06.alt: Suloko, the Ascension of our Lord: Holy Qurbono for the people. Ten days of prayer for the coming of the Holy Spirit follow; according to the lectionary, marriages are not celebrated in these days.
2027-05-06.verse: While he was blessing them, he withdrew from them and was carried up into heaven.
theo: Forty days after his Resurrection, Jesus leads his disciples out to Bethany, “and, lifting up his hands, he blessed them. While he was blessing them, he withdrew from them and was carried up into heaven.” The last earthly sight of Jesus is of hands raised in blessing. He goes, but he does not stop blessing his Church.

The Ascension is not Jesus leaving us; it is our humanity entering heaven. The Son of God, who took our flesh, now takes it to the right hand of the Father. St Mark says: “he was taken up into heaven and sat down at the right hand of God.” Where the Head has gone, the body hopes to follow. Our true home is with him.

The angels ask the disciples: “Men of Galilee, why do you stand looking up toward heaven? This Jesus… will come in the same way as you saw him go.” The Ascension is not a time for gazing at the sky but for mission: “Go into all the world and proclaim the good news to the whole creation… And they went out and proclaimed the good news everywhere, while the Lord worked with them.”

As Elijah was taken up and Elisha received his mantle and spirit, so Christ ascends and pours out his Spirit on his Church. Jeremiah's promise will be fulfilled at Pentecost: “I will put my law within them, and I will write it on their hearts.” Like the disciples, who “returned to Jerusalem with great joy and were continually in the temple blessing God”, we now enter ten days of prayer for the Spirit.
conn: 2 Kings 2:13–15: Elisha takes the mantle of the ascended Elijah and receives his spirit: a figure of the Church receiving Christ's Spirit.
Deuteronomy 10:1–5: the tablets placed in the ark; Jeremiah 31:33: the law written on hearts by the Spirit.
Ephesians 4:8–11: the ascended Christ gives apostles, prophets, evangelists, pastors and teachers to build up his body.
Isaiah 49:6 and Acts 1:8: the mission goes to the ends of the earth.
altar: At every Holy Qurbono we are invited: “Lift up your hearts”, and we answer, “They are with the Lord.” The ascended Christ, seated at the Father's right hand, comes down to us on the altar, and lifts us up to him.
outline: Hands raised in blessing: the last sight of Jesus.
Where the Head has gone, the body will follow.
The Spirit given to the Church.
With Mary and the apostles, waiting for Pentecost.
live: Pray each day until Pentecost: “Come, Holy Spirit.”
Share the Good News with one person this week, in word or deed.
At the Qurbono, really lift up your heart to the Lord at “Lift up your hearts”.
fathers: “Christ's Ascension is our elevation; where the glory of the Head has gone before, there the hope of the body is called to follow” (Sermon 73 on the Ascension, 4).

“Today our Lord Jesus Christ ascended into heaven; let our hearts ascend with him… He did not leave heaven when he came down to us; nor did he withdraw from us when he went up again into heaven” (Sermon on the Ascension, Mai 98).
magis: Christ's Ascension marks the definitive entrance of Jesus' humanity into God's heavenly domain; he precedes us so that we might live in hope of following.
The heavenly liturgy: the ascended Christ is the high priest of the true sanctuary.
The disciples, with Mary, persevered in prayer awaiting the Spirit.
saints: Sunday 9 May: VI Sunday after Qyomtho. Sunday 16 May: Pentecost.
2027-05-06.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, ascended into heaven, you raised your hands to bless your disciples and took our humanity to the Father's right hand. Bless us from heaven, lift up our hearts to you, send us to proclaim your Gospel, and pour out your Spirit on your Church. Amen.

quick: Jesus ascends with hands raised in blessing.
Our humanity has entered heaven: where the Head is, the body hopes to follow.
Not gazing upwards, but going out: the Ascension leads to mission.
2027-05-06.action: Pray every day until Pentecost: “Come, Holy Spirit.”
2027-05-06.question: Is my heart lifted up to the Lord, or only looking at earthly things?
2027-05-06.special: Suloko, the Ascension of our Lord: day of obligation; Holy Qurbono for the people. Ten days of prayer until Pentecost (no marriage celebrations, as in the lectionary).
illus: When a Kerala father leaves for work abroad, the family gathers at the door and he raises his hand to bless the children before the car leaves. They remember that blessing for months. Jesus left his disciples with his hands raised in blessing, and he has never lowered them.

family.explain: Forty days after Easter, Jesus blessed his friends and went up to heaven. He is with God the Father, and he still blesses us. He promised to send the Holy Spirit.
family.intention: We pray for families separated by work abroad, and for the coming of the Holy Spirit.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we pray together for the Holy Spirit these ten days?”

kidsaint: When his teacher Elijah was taken up to heaven, Elisha picked up his cloak and received his spirit to carry on God's work. Lesson: when Jesus went to heaven, he gave us his Spirit to continue his work.
term: Syriac for “ascension”: the feast of the Ascension of our Lord, forty days after Qyomtho, always on a Thursday.
termMore: Between the Ascension and Pentecost the Church prays, like the apostles with Mary in the upper room (Acts 1:14), for the coming of the Holy Spirit.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, forty days after Easter Jesus leads his disciples out to Bethany. He lifts up his hands and blesses them, and while he is blessing them he is carried up into heaven. The last picture the disciples have of Jesus is of hands raised in blessing. He has never lowered them.

The Ascension does not mean that Jesus has gone far away. It means that our human nature, which he took from Mary, now sits at the right hand of the Father. Where he, our Head, has gone, we, his body, hope to follow. Heaven is our home.

But the angels say: “Men of Galilee, why do you stand looking up toward heaven?” The Ascension is not a time for gazing at the sky; it is a time for mission. Jesus said: “Go into all the world and proclaim the good news.” And they went out and preached everywhere, and the Lord worked with them.

Elijah was taken up, and Elisha received his mantle and his spirit. Jesus ascends, and he will send his Spirit upon us at Pentecost. Like the apostles with Mary, let us spend these ten days in prayer: Come, Holy Spirit. And at every Qurbono, when we hear “Lift up your hearts,” let us truly lift them up to him. Amen.
kids: Children, today Jesus went up to heaven! He took his friends to a hill, raised his hands and blessed them, and then went up into the sky until a cloud hid him.
Jesus is now with God the Father, but he still blesses us and loves us. And he promised to send the Holy Spirit to help us.
For the next ten days, let's pray every day: “Come, Holy Spirit!”

intro: Theme: “He was carried up into heaven, blessing them.”
Forty days after his Resurrection the Lord ascends. It is not a farewell of absence but of glory: our human nature, in Christ, enters heaven, and the Church is sent to the ends of the earth.

sub: Elijah was taken up in a whirlwind; Elisha received his spirit.
Jesus lifts up his hands and blesses the disciples; while blessing them he is carried up.
His last gesture on earth is blessing: his hands remain raised over the Church.
q: As they continued walking and talking, a chariot of fire and horses of fire separated the two of them, and Elijah ascended in a whirlwind into heaven.
Then he led them out as far as Bethany, and, lifting up his hands, he blessed them. While he was blessing them, he withdrew from them and was carried up into heaven.
points.apply: Receive the final blessing at every Qurbono as Christ's own blessing.

points.h: Seated at the right hand of the Father
sub: The Psalm foretold: “Sit at my right hand.”
Christ, true God and true man, takes our humanity into the glory of the Father.
There he intercedes for us as our High Priest; where the Head has gone, the members hope to follow (CCC 661–667).
q: The LORD says to my lord, “Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies your footstool.”
So then the Lord Jesus, after he had spoken to them, was taken up into heaven and sat down at the right hand of God.
points.apply: Lift your heart to heaven each day: “Lord, draw me to where you are.”

points.h: Why stand looking up? Be witnesses
sub: The prophets saw that the spirit of Elijah rested on Elisha.
The angels ask: “Why do you stand looking up toward heaven?” He will come again.
Meanwhile, with the power of the Spirit, we are witnesses to the ends of the earth.
q: When the company of prophets who were at Jericho saw him at a distance, they declared, “The spirit of Elijah rests on Elisha.”
But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you; and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, in all Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth.
points.apply: Begin the novena to the Holy Spirit with Mary, from tomorrow until Pentecost.

concl: The Ascension is the feast of our hope: our humanity is in heaven with Christ.
Let us return like the apostles “with great joy”, praying with Mary for the Spirit.
2027-05-06.resolve: Pray the novena to the Holy Spirit from the Ascension to Pentecost.
